title: leanprof elab: one module of a dataset (version 1)
description: Written by `leanprof elab` for each profiled file to DATASET/modules/MODULE.json. Amounts are whole nanoseconds, or heartbeats when unit is "heartbeats". Fields may be added in later versions of the same major version; consumers must ignore unknown fields.

file.description: the source file, relative to the project

lean_version.description: Lean.versionString of the Lean that elaborated it; empty without the driver

exact_ranges.description: elaborated by leanprof-elab-driver: terms and tactics by exact source range, and a timeline

compact.description: --compact: commands, terms and tactics only, not the operations inside them

threshold.description: operations other than terms and tactics under this (ms, or heartbeats) are not recorded on their own

term_threshold.description: terms and tactics under this are not recorded on their own; 0: every one is

wall_ns.description: wall time of the process that elaborated the file, imports included

imports_ns.description: loading the imports, as the driver measured it; 0 without the driver

total.description: the sum of the file's commands' traced cost (Lean elaborates on several threads: can exceed wall_ns)

ranges.description: every term and tactic, by exact source range, costliest first

range.description: line:col-line:col; lines and columns count from 1, and the end column is one past the range's last character

text.description: the source, whitespace collapsed, at most 100 characters

amount.description: inclusive cost; a range nested in itself (a macro's expansion) counted once

count.description: how many times it was elaborated

events.description: the timeline: every recorded operation (empty with heartbeats or without the driver)

prefixItems.description: index of the operation it ran in, -1 for a root (a command, or work Lean ran asynchronously)
start, ns after the driver started
line:col-line:col for a term or tactic (Leanprof.term, Leanprof.tactic), else null
a term or tactic's syntax kind (short), a command's source, or the operation's description
